questions.q: What did Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 52 already cover in full, according to this lesson?
options: The @dp.expect, @dp.expect_or_drop, and @dp.expect_or_fail Python decorators for Expectations
The SQL CONSTRAINT syntax for Expectations
Databricks Asset Bundles
The Workflows UI's visual DAG editor
questions.explain: This lesson explicitly builds on Lesson 52's Python coverage rather than re-teaching it, adding the SQL equivalent instead.

questions.q: What is the SQL equivalent of Lesson 52's @dp.expect_or_drop?
options: CONSTRAINT name EXPECT (expr) ON VIOLATION DROP ROW
CONSTRAINT name EXPECT (expr) ON VIOLATION FAIL UPDATE
DROP CONSTRAINT name
CONSTRAINT name WARN (expr)
questions.explain: ON VIOLATION DROP ROW filters out violating rows before they reach the table — the same outcome as expect_or_drop.

questions.q: What happens to a row that violates a CONSTRAINT with no ON VIOLATION clause specified?
options: The row is kept in the table, and the violation is counted (the default warn behavior)
The row is immediately dropped
The entire pipeline run fails
The row is moved to an automatic quarantine table
questions.explain: EXPECT alone, with no ON VIOLATION clause, defaults to warn — the same as the bare @dp.expect decorator.

questions.q: Why does this lesson describe Expectations as a genuinely different mechanism from a manual quality-check step (Lesson 36)?
options: Because the constraint lives inside the table's own definition, so it can never drift out of sync with the transformation
Because Expectations are slower than a manual check
Because Expectations can only be used in Python, never SQL
Because Expectations require a separate quarantine table by default
questions.explain: A manual check is a separate query maintained by hand; a CONSTRAINT/@dp.expect rule is part of the same statement as the transformation.

questions.q: Does ON VIOLATION DROP ROW automatically redirect dropped rows to a quarantine table?
options: No — the row is simply excluded; a real quarantine pattern requires a separate, deliberately designed table
Yes — every dropped row is automatically captured in a quarantine table
Yes, but only for materialized views, never streaming tables
Dropped rows are always written to a system-managed error log automatically
questions.explain: A dropped row is excluded, not redirected — building an actual quarantine pattern is a separate, deliberate design choice.
